chunk_findings.detail: `fsio.rmtree_owned` raises `ValueError` (empty, relative, cwd, or filesystem root) and can also raise from `Path.resolve()` (symlink loop), while the previous `shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True)` did not raise. That call sits in a `finally` after `return rehearsal.run(), rehearsal`. If `work` is `Path('')`, `Path('.')`, `Path.cwd()`, or `Path('/')`, or `resolve()` fails, the `finally` exception discards a successful return and replaces whatever `rehearsal.run()` raised, so the dry-run result never reaches the caller.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/upgrade_dryrun/_drive.py:27

chunk_findings.detail: The surrounding handler is documented as never raising: a failed removal must be left for `cleanup` to name and prune, and this handler is the only cleanup. `fsio.rmtree_owned(tree)` raises `ValueError` before `ignore_errors` applies. Given `tree` equal to `Path('.')`, `Path('')`, `Path.cwd()`, or `Path('/')` (plausible if the process’s cwd is the worktree being torn down), the handler raises and the later `worktree prune` does not run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/scratch.py:73

chunk_findings.detail: The loop’s next line treats a refused removal as non-fatal (`if not old.exists()` then it is not recorded). `rmtree_owned(old)` does not return on refusal; it raises. One relative doomed path (for example `Path('.ddflow/backups/old-tag')` when the repo root was not made absolute) or a path that resolves to the cwd aborts the sweep, so later doomed trees are not removed and the function does not return the removals already done.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/backups.py:113

chunk_findings.detail: The previous ValueError leak is gone for the default `ignore_errors=True`, but that fix does not cover resolution failures. `resolved = p.resolve()` and `Path.cwd().resolve()` sit outside any handler, so a symlink loop still raises `RuntimeError` before the `elif not ignore_errors` branch. Given `work` or `tree` equal to an absolute path whose resolution cycles (or a cwd that does), `upgrade_dryrun/_drive.py`’s `finally` still replaces a successful `rehearsal.run()` result, and `ci/scratch.py`’s handler, which is documented as never raising, still aborts before `worktree prune`.

chunk_findings.detail: `rmtree_owned` always calls `p.resolve()` and `Path.cwd().resolve()` before it consults `ignore_errors`, and it does not catch the errors those calls raise. Given an absolute owned target such as `Path('/tmp/legit-tree')` with the default `ignore_errors=True`, if the process cwd has been unlinked, `Path.cwd()` raises `FileNotFoundError` and the tree is never removed. The same leak happens when a path component is not a directory (`NotADirectoryError` from `resolve()`) or is a symlink loop. Callers that previously used `shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True)`, including the scratch handler documented as never raising, now abort and skip later cleanup.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/fsio.py:rmtree_owned

chunk_findings.detail: `test_refuses_an_empty_path_silently_by_default` only asserts `Path.cwd() == tmp_path` after `fsio.rmtree_owned("")`. The failure mode the module docstring names is that `shutil.rmtree('', ignore_errors=True)` empties the cwd (children gone, directory inode still there), so cwd identity is unchanged and this assertion still holds. With a marker file in `tmp_path`, an unfixed call that deletes that marker still passes, so the test does not fail against the unfixed code the change claims to regress.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_rmtree_owned.py:22

chunk_findings.detail: The previous cwd leak is not fixed. `resolved, cwd = p.resolve(), Path.cwd().resolve()` is one expression, and any `OSError` from `Path.cwd()` (cwd unlinked → `FileNotFoundError`) is treated as “target cannot be resolved”. Given an absolute owned tree such as `Path('/tmp/legit-tree')` and the default `ignore_errors=True`, a missing cwd sets `reason`, `refuse` returns, and `rmtree` is never called, so the tree is left in place even though only the cwd lookup failed.

Given `work` or `tree` equal to an absolute path whose resolution cycles (or a cwd that does), `upgrade_dryrun/_drive.py`’s `finally` still replaces a successful `rehearsal.run()` result, and `ci/scratch.py`’s handler, which is documented as never raising, still aborts before `worktree prune`.

chunk_findings.detail: `p.resolve()` (and `Path.cwd().resolve()`) can raise `RuntimeError` on a symlink loop on Python versions before 3.13; `RuntimeError` is not an `OSError`, so the new handler never runs. With the default `ignore_errors=True`, `rmtree_owned` on an absolute path that cycles (or a cwd that does) still aborts instead of refusing silently, and with `ignore_errors=False` it raises `RuntimeError` rather than the documented `ValueError`. A `finally` caller such as a dry-run cleanup still loses a successful result to that leak.
